@ when~(v != 0) runs the counter where the last event is not 0: false before the first event, the output kept on the stopped frames
@ a delay, a grid of sample / 2 and a part with a Default of its own under when~(v != 0) count the runs: the output is T.default() before the first run
@ a condition made of the event before the last one is read where the call is written: after the maker it has the event of the frame, above it the one before
@ a when~ in a flow of its own with the event passed in, a let of the level, with and without at sample, give the values of the direct form
@ when~(v != 0).when~(g) runs where both hold, as does when~(v != 0 && g): the frames 2 and 7
process 0 frames=12 in x=[2 2 1 2 0 2 2 1 0 2 2 2] g=[true true true false true true false true true true false true]
process 1 frames=12 in x=[2 2 1 2 0 2 2 1 0 2 2 2] g=[true true true false true true false true true true false true]
@ when~(c).reset_if~(r) resets also on the stopped frames and puts the kept output back; reset_if~(r).when~(c) resets only on the frames that run
process 0 frames=12 in x=[2 2 1 2 0 2 2 1 0 2 2 2] r=[false false false true false true false false false false false false]
process 1 frames=12 in x=[2 2 1 2 0 2 2 1 0 2 2 2] r=[false false false true false true false false false false false false]
@ the calls of process cut the frames anywhere, a call of 0 frames too: the last event and the runs are in the state
@ reset puts the last event (no event: the level is false), the runs and the kept output back
